analysis.title: United Parcel Service Inc. (UPS): 3Q26 EPS Beat; Domestic Margin On Track; Further Upside from Intl Margin Trajectory
key_insights: UPS reported 3Q26 adjusted EPS of $1.69 vs GS/Visible Alpha consensus of $1.62/$1.63, up 17% y/y. The beat came from stronger revenue per piece (RPP) in Domestic, Domestic margin in line at the 7% guide, and stronger International margins.

Domestic revenue per piece grew 6.1% vs cost per piece growth of 5.3%, a spread of 84bps inside UPS's 50-100bp target range. GS reads this as the first sign of improved Domestic profitability over 2H26 y/y after the Amazon volume drawdown completed in 2Q26.
Domestic margin of 7% matched GS and consensus despite higher fuel prices. Domestic EBIT dollars were 4% above GS's forecast on slightly better volumes, helped by core volumes ex-Amazon.

International margin was 14.9% vs GS 13.5% and consensus 13.5%, above the guided 13%-14% range. GS attributes the 140bps beat to stronger volume in higher-margin tradelanes such as China to US and Asia to Asia.

GS calls this the start of UPS's 'prove it' story. The bank says consistent quarters of Domestic margin improvement and a typical peak season are probably needed before investors gain full confidence in the turnaround.
UPS shares are up 1% YTD vs the transport group up 22%. GS says margin and volume recovery, particularly core volumes ex-Amazon (up nearly 2% in 3Q), could catalyze the shares.

4Q26 guide implies a large International margin step-up to ~20% (from 14.9% in 3Q) that is needed to hit full-year expectations. GS expects it to come mainly from higher surcharges reflected in yields and growth in higher-margin lanes.

FY26 guidance was raised: revenue to ~$92.6B (from ~$91.2B; GSe $91.9B, VA consensus $91.6B), EBIT ~$8.75B or ~9.4% margin (from 9.5%), EPS ~$7.28 (from $7.22; GSe $7.20, VA consensus $7.19), free cash flow ~$6.1B (from ~$5.5B).
4Q26 guide: revenue ~$25.7B, EBIT ~$3.3B, Domestic revenue +~3% y/y at ~10.5% margin, International revenue +~7% at ~20% margin, SCS revenue up nearly 13% at ~12.2% margin.

Domestic volume fell 3.3% y/y (Ground -2.7%, Deferred -6.1%, Next Day -7%). Average revenue per piece rose 6.1%, with about half from base rate and customer mix and the rest from higher fuel surcharge.

SMB mix rose to 35.1% of volume from 32.8% a year earlier, with SMB volumes up 3.7%. B2B volumes stayed negative, but UPS cited growth in healthcare (~6% a year), automotive, and data centers (could double off a small base, up to a longer-term $15B opportunity).
International volume fell 8.7% y/y (International Domestic -9.1%, Export -8.3%) while yield rose 15.1% vs GS's 12.4%. SCS EBIT was 9% below GS's forecast on 6% higher revenue.

GS raised FY26 EPS by $0.08 to $7.28, FY27 by $0.05 to $8.20, and FY28 and FY29 by $0.10 each to $9.10 and $10.10. The change comes from higher International margin (FY26 International margin raised to 20%) with Domestic margin unchanged at 10.5%.

Teamster wages are contractually set to rise 4.8% in August 2027 from 2.2% in 2026, which could pressure the RPP-CPP spread in 2H27. GS says a 78,000 headcount reduction over 2025-2026, including 7,500 Teamsters, should help absorb it.
Buy rating on the Conviction List maintained. 12-month price target raised to $135 from $132, based on ~15.5x P/E (unchanged) on Q5-Q8 EPS of $8.83, implying 34.6% upside from $100.32.

market_movers.rationale: Price target raised from $132 after the 3Q26 beat and higher International margin outlook. The stock stays on the Conviction List, with 34.6% upside to the target.

sector_views.rationale: UPS is one of three global integrated time-definite networks (with FDX and DHL), and a leaner cost base should deliver better margins over time with price discipline and freight volume recovery.

earnings_insights: UPS 3Q26 adjusted EPS reported $1.69 vs GS/Visible Alpha consensus estimate $1.62/$1.63, up 17% y/y. GS had estimated $1.63 (a $0.06 beat per GS).
3Q26 Domestic revenue reported ~$14.9B, 4% above GS estimate, with Domestic margin 7% vs GS and consensus estimate 7.0%.
3Q26 International revenue reported $5B, 1% above GS estimate, with margin 14.9% vs GS estimate 13.5% and consensus estimate 13.5%.
3Q26 total operating revenue reported $22.9B vs GS estimate $22B, with consolidated margin 9.0% vs GS estimate 8.9%.
FY26 company guidance: revenue ~$92.6B, EBIT ~$8.75B (~9.4% margin), EPS ~$7.28, FCF ~$6.1B, capex ~$3.0B, dividends ~$5.4B, tax rate ~23.0%.
GS 4Q26 EPS forecast is $2.77, with 1Q27E at $1.45 and 2Q27E at $1.96.

trade_ideas.description: Buy UPS, Conviction List, 12-month price target $135
trade_ideas.rationale: Domestic margin repair with RPP above CPP and an International margin step-up should drive earnings growth through 2027-2029.
trade_ideas.risk: Economic slowdown and tariff impacts on freight, Amazon volume exit or competition, Teamster wage increases and labor negotiations, execution on Network of the Future.

risk_factors: Material economic slowdown, including tariff impacts on global freight flows.
New entrants and peak season disruptions.
Ability to absorb higher costs from the Teamster labor contract and the next labor negotiation.
Execution on Network of the Future, the new USPS contract and GroundSaver insourcing.
Remaining Amazon volumes and whether they exit after 2H26, plus Amazon as a potential competitor.
Inability to adjust costs in time to the Amazon volume exit, and execution of the multi-year network reconfiguration and cost takeout plan.
4Q26 International margin must step up meaningfully to meet full-year guidance.
geopolitical: Tariff impacts on global freight flows are cited as a downside risk to UPS.
cross_bank_references: GS notes UPS is one of three global integrated time-definite players, along with FDX and DHL.

tension_points.bull_case: Domestic RPP is growing above CPP within the 50-100bp range, core volumes ex-Amazon turned positive (up nearly 2%), SMB mix is rising, and International margin of 14.9% beat guidance. GS sees earnings growth accelerating in 2027 and compounding in 2028-2029.
tension_points.bear_case: UPS must still show consistent Domestic margin gains and a clean peak season, deliver a large 4Q International margin step-up to ~20%, and handle Amazon overhangs and Teamster wage increases of 4.8% in August 2027. B2B volumes remain negative.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A miss on the ~20% 4Q26 International margin or ~10.5% Domestic margin guide, or an RPP-CPP spread falling below the 50-100bp range, would undercut the turnaround thesis.

theme_stances.key_argument: With the Amazon drawdown complete, higher-quality revenue over a lower cost-to-serve network should produce a 50-100bp RPP-CPP spread and steady Domestic margin expansion.
theme_stances.evidence: RPP growth of 6.1% was above CPP growth of 5.3%

theme_stances.key_argument: Stronger volume in higher-margin lanes and higher surcharges lift International margin toward 20% in 4Q26, with potential further upside into 2027.
theme_stances.evidence: strong 4Q26 margin outlook, could prove to have additional upside into 2027
